lead: Cisco's professional-level networking cert, for engineers who build and run campus and enterprise networks. You pass two exams: the ENCOR core exam and one concentration of your choice. ENCOR moved to version 1.2 on March 19, 2026: wireless moved out to the new CCNP Wireless, and AI joined automation.
objSub: The six domains of the ENCOR v1.2 core exam. Tick topics as you study them; progress saves on this device. The concentration exams are listed in the cards below.
planSub: Set how many hours a week you can give it. The plan covers the ENCOR core exam's six domains by weight, then saves time for practice. Budget extra time for your concentration exam after that.

v12.label: ENCOR v1.2
v12.note: The core exam. Passing it alone earns Cisco Certified Specialist – Enterprise Core and qualifies you for the CCIE Enterprise Infrastructure lab. Version 1.2 removed wireless (now in CCNP Wireless, core exam 350-101 WLCOR) and renamed domain 6 Automation and Artificial Intelligence. The last day for v1.1 was March 18, 2026.
v12.onote: Topic titles from Cisco's 350-401 ENCOR v1.2 exam topics. The line under each lists its sub-topics in plain language.

domains.name: Architecture
obj: Explain the different design principles used in an enterprise network
2-tier, 3-tier, fabric and cloud designs, and high availability with redundancy, FHRP and SSO.
Explain the working principles of the Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN solution
Control and data plane parts, and the benefits and limits of SD-WAN.
Explain the working principles of the Cisco SD-Access solution
Control and data plane parts, and how a traditional campus works alongside SD-Access.
Interpret QoS configurations
Read a QoS policy: classification, marking, queuing, policing and shaping.

domains.name: Virtualization
obj: Describe device virtualization technologies
Type 1 and Type 2 hypervisors, virtual machines and virtual switching.
Configure and verify data path virtualization technologies
VRFs, and GRE and IPsec tunnels.
Describe network virtualization concepts
LISP and VXLAN.

domains.name: Infrastructure
obj: Layer 2
Troubleshoot 802.1Q trunks and EtherChannels; configure and verify RSTP and MST with root guard and BPDU guard.
Layer 3
Compare EIGRP and OSPF; configure OSPFv2 and v3 (areas, summarization, filtering, network types, passive interfaces); configure eBGP between direct neighbors; describe policy-based routing.
IP Services
Read NTP and PTP configs; configure NAT and PAT; configure HSRP and VRRP; describe multicast (RPF, PIM-SM, IGMP v2 and v3, SSM, bidir, MSDP).

domains.name: Network Assurance
obj: Diagnose network problems using tools such as debugs, conditional debugs, traceroute, ping, SNMP and syslog
Find the fault with the right tool, without flooding the router.
Configure and verify Flexible NetFlow
Records of who talked to whom, how much and when.
Configure SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
Copy traffic from ports or VLANs to a capture tool, locally or across the network.
Configure and verify IPSLA
Probe paths and services and react when they degrade.
Describe how Cisco Catalyst Center is used to apply network configuration, monitoring and management
Formerly DNA Center. Traditional and AI-powered workflows.
Configure and verify NETCONF and RESTCONF
Model-driven management over SSH or HTTPS.

domains.name: Security
obj: Configure and verify device access control
Line passwords and local users, and AAA authentication and authorization.
Configure and verify infrastructure security features
ACLs (standard, extended, named, time-based) and control plane policing (CoPP).
Describe REST API security
Authentication, tokens, HTTPS and protecting API access.
Describe the components of network security design
Threat defense, endpoint security, next-generation firewalls, TrustSec and MACsec.

domains.name: Automation and Artificial Intelligence
obj: Interpret basic Python components and scripts
Variables, loops, functions and libraries in short network scripts.
Construct valid JSON-encoded files
Objects, arrays, strings and numbers, with correct quotes and commas.
Describe the high-level principles and benefits of a data modeling language, such as YANG
Why models make automation predictable.
Describe APIs for Cisco Catalyst Center and SD-WAN Manager
Northbound REST APIs for automation and reporting.
Interpret REST API response codes and results in payload using Cisco Catalyst Center and RESTCONF
200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404 and 500, and what the payload says.
Construct an EEM applet to automate configuration, troubleshooting or data collection
Embedded Event Manager: trigger on an event, then run actions on the router.
Compare agent vs. agentless orchestration tools
Tools that need software on each device vs ones that use SSH or APIs.

extras.title: Concentration exams (pick one)
rows: The most common pick: OSPF, EIGRP and BGP troubleshooting, route maps, VPN services and infrastructure security.
Design-focused: addressing, routing, campus, WAN and SD-Access design.
Python, APIs and controllers. Also counts toward CCNP Automation.
Connecting enterprise networks to public cloud.
Monitoring and assurance tools for enterprise networks.
Now in the separate CCNP Wireless track, with core exam 350-101 WLCOR.

extras.title: How the cert adds up
rows: Also earns Specialist – Enterprise Core and the CCIE Enterprise lab ticket.
Each one also earns its own Specialist cert.
After you pass one, you have 3 years to pass the other.

extras.title: Admin distance
rows: A directly connected network always wins.
Routes learned from an external BGP peer.
Routes from inside the EIGRP domain.
Routes from an internal BGP peer.

extras.title: STP guards
rows: Access ports skip listening and learning. Edge ports only.
Err-disables an edge port if a switch shows up there.
Blocks a port that tries to become the path to a new root.
Keeps a port blocked if BPDUs stop arriving.

method: Infrastructure is 30% of ENCOR. Start with Layer 2 and Layer 3, then security, then automation.
Build topologies in Cisco Packet Tracer (free) or Cisco Modeling Labs. Configure every 'configure and verify' topic until you can do it without notes.
Mismatch an OSPF area, a trunk's allowed VLANs or an HSRP priority on purpose, then fix it with show and debug commands.
Flashcards for admin distances, OSPF LSA and network types, STP features, REST response codes and JSON syntax.
Choose your concentration early. ENARSI pairs naturally with ENCOR because it goes deeper on the same routing.
tips: Many questions show a show command or a config. Find the one line that matters before reading the answers.
Default timers, priorities and admin distances decide a lot of answers.
Cisco exams don't let you return to a question once you move on. Answer, then move.
Python, JSON and REST codes are 15% and easy points if you practice them.

items: The core and concentration exams and official courses.
CCNP Enterprise ENCOR Official Cert Guide
The official book for the core exam.
Free simulator for trunks, STP, OSPF, HSRP and ACLs.
Real IOS XE images on your own PC. The free tier allows a few nodes.
Try Catalyst Center, RESTCONF and NETCONF APIs on Cisco's lab gear.

quiz.q: A campus has an access layer and a combined distribution and core layer. Which design is this?
o: A two-tier, collapsed core design
Right. Distribution and core are merged into one layer, which fits small and medium campuses.
A three-tier design
Three-tier keeps access, distribution and core as separate layers.
A leaf-spine fabric
Leaf-spine is a data center fabric where every leaf connects to every spine.
A hub-and-spoke WAN
That describes how sites connect over the WAN, not the campus layers.

quiz.q: In Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, which component builds the secure control connections and distributes routes and policy to the edge routers?
o: SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart)
Right. The controller is the control plane: it uses OMP to send routes and policy to WAN edges.
SD-WAN Validator (formerly vBond)
The validator handles first authentication and orchestration, then points devices to the controllers.
SD-WAN Manager (formerly vManage)
Manager is the management plane: GUI, templates and monitoring.
The WAN edge router
The edge router forwards traffic in the data plane.

quiz.q: Two customers on one router both use 10.1.1.0/24, and their traffic must never mix. What should you configure?
o: A separate VRF for each customer
Right. Each VRF has its own routing table, so overlapping addresses don't clash.
Two VLANs with the same SVI
An SVI belongs to one routing table. Overlapping subnets would still clash.
NAT on the outside interface
NAT can hide addresses but doesn't separate the routing tables.
A GRE tunnel between the customers
A tunnel would connect them, the opposite of what you want.

quiz.q: Which technology carries Layer 2 frames across a Layer 3 network inside UDP?
o: VXLAN
Right. VXLAN wraps Layer 2 frames in UDP, with a 24-bit VNI that allows about 16 million segments.
LISP
LISP separates where a host is from who it is. It isn't a Layer 2 overlay.
802.1Q tags VLANs on a trunk; it doesn't cross a routed network.
IPsec
IPsec encrypts IP packets. On its own it doesn't carry Layer 2 frames.

quiz.q: A router learns 10.20.0.0/16 from OSPF and 10.20.5.0/24 from EIGRP. A packet heads to 10.20.5.9. Which route is used?
o: The EIGRP /24, because the longest prefix match wins
Right. The router picks the most specific route first. Admin distance only breaks ties between identical prefixes.
The OSPF /16, because OSPF is more common
Popularity doesn't matter. Prefix length decides.
Whichever has the lower metric
Metrics are only compared within one protocol.
Both, with load balancing
Different prefix lengths are different routes; they don't load-balance.

quiz.q: Two OSPF routers on the same Ethernet segment stay stuck in INIT/2WAY and never reach FULL. Hello timers match. What is a common cause?
o: Mismatched MTU or network type
Right. An MTU mismatch stalls the database exchange, and a network type mismatch breaks how adjacencies form.
Different router IDs
Router IDs must be different. Matching IDs would be the problem.
Different process IDs
OSPF process IDs are local and don't have to match.
A missing default route
A default route has nothing to do with forming an adjacency.

quiz.q: Two routers run HSRP for a gateway. R1 has priority 110 and R2 has the default. R1 fails and comes back, but R2 stays active. Why?
o: Preempt isn't enabled on R1
Right. Without preempt, a higher-priority router won't take the active role back. Add standby preempt.
R2's priority is higher
The default HSRP priority is 100, lower than 110.
HSRP doesn't support priorities
It does: priority picks the active router.
The virtual MAC changed
The virtual MAC stays the same either way. It doesn't decide which router is active.

quiz.q: An access port connects one user PC. Which pair of features is BEST for it?
o: PortFast and BPDU guard
Right. PortFast brings the port up fast, and BPDU guard shuts it down if someone plugs in a switch.
Root guard and trunking
Root guard is for distribution ports facing downstream switches, and a PC doesn't need a trunk.
Loop guard and EtherChannel
These are for switch-to-switch links.
UDLD and a native VLAN change
UDLD finds one-way fiber links; it's not the access-port pair the exam expects.

quiz.q: Security wants every packet from a server's switch port copied to a capture box in another building, across the routed network. What should you configure?
o: ERSPAN
Right. ERSPAN wraps mirrored traffic in GRE so it can cross Layer 3 to a remote collector.
Local SPAN
Local SPAN only copies to a port on the same switch.
RSPAN
RSPAN uses a special VLAN and can't cross a routed boundary.
NetFlow
NetFlow sends flow records, not full packet copies.

quiz.q: You need to debug OSPF on a busy core router without flooding the console. What should you use?
o: A conditional debug limited to one interface or neighbor
Right. Conditional debugs limit output to what you care about, protecting the CPU.
debug all
That can overload the router and drop traffic.
Turn off logging
Then you'd see nothing at all.
Reboot the router first
A reboot clears the problem you're trying to observe and causes an outage.

quiz.q: You want admins to log in to switches with their own accounts checked against a central server, with every command logged. What should you configure?
o: AAA with TACACS+
Right. TACACS+ separates authentication, authorization and accounting, and can log each command.
A shared enable secret
A shared password hides who did what.
Local users on every switch
That doesn't scale and has no central command log.
Telnet on the VTY lines
Telnet sends credentials in clear text. Use SSH.

quiz.q: A router's CPU spikes during a flood of traffic aimed at the router itself. Which feature protects the control plane?
o: Control plane policing (CoPP)
Right. CoPP rate-limits traffic headed to the router's CPU, so routing protocols and management stay up.
An ACL on the outside interface only
An interface ACL helps but doesn't protect against everything aimed at the control plane.
QoS marking
Marking labels traffic. It doesn't limit what reaches the CPU.
Port security
Port security limits MAC addresses on switch access ports.

quiz.q: Which of these is valid JSON?
o: A
Right. Keys and strings use double quotes, and there's no trailing comma.
B
JSON doesn't allow single quotes.
C
JSON doesn't allow a trailing comma before the closing brace.
D
Keys must be in double quotes.

quiz.q: A RESTCONF request to create a new interface returns 201. What does that mean?
o: Created: the new resource was made
Right. 201 means the request succeeded and created something.
Unauthorized
That's 401.
Not found
That's 404.
Server error
That's 500.

quiz.q: Which statement about agentless orchestration tools is true?
o: They reach devices over existing protocols like SSH or APIs, with no software installed on the device
Right. That's why they're common for network gear, which often can't run an agent.
They need an agent installed on every device
That's agent-based tools.
They only work on Windows servers
Agentless tools manage network devices and servers of many kinds.
They can't push configuration changes
Pushing configuration is their main job.

pbqs.title: Find the fault in the output
pbqs.scenario: Six network tickets came with command output. Pick the cause each one shows. Each answer is used once; two options are distractors.

items.log:
%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch
 discovered on GigabitEthernet1/0/24 (1), with SW2 Gi1/0/24 (99).
items.why: The two ends of the trunk use different native VLANs. Make them match on both sides.

items.log:
Group  Port-channel  Protocol  Ports
1      Po1(SD)       LACP      Gi1/0/1(I) Gi1/0/2(I)
# SW3 side: channel-group 1 mode on
items.why: One side runs LACP and the other is forced on, so the ports stay individual (I). Use LACP on both ends.

items.log:
%OSPF-4-ERRRCV: Received invalid packet: mismatched area ID
 from backbone area must be virtual-link but not found
 from 10.1.12.2, GigabitEthernet0/1
items.why: The neighbors put the shared link in different areas. Put both interfaces in the same area.

items.log:
Interface  Grp  Pri P State    Active    Standby
Gi0/0      10   120   Standby  10.1.1.3  local
# R1 is back up after a reboot
items.why: R1 has the higher priority but no P flag, so it won't take back the active role. Add preempt.

items.log:
(empty)
# config:
interface Gi0/0  ! LAN
 ip nat outside
interface Gi0/1  ! ISP
 ip nat inside
items.why: The LAN side is marked outside and the ISP side inside, so nothing matches. Swap them.

items.log:
Extended IP access list EDGE-IN
 10 deny tcp any host 10.5.5.10 eq 443 (1874 matches)
 20 permit ip any any
items.why: Line 10 is denying HTTPS to the web server, and its hit count shows it's matching. Fix or remove it.

pbqs.title: Pick the feature and the domain
pbqs.scenario: For each requirement, pick the feature that meets it and the ENCOR domain it belongs to. Some options aren't used.

rows.req: Keep two tenants' overlapping subnets separate on one router
rows.why: VRFs give each tenant its own routing table.

rows.req: Run fewer spanning-tree instances by grouping VLANs
rows.why: MST maps many VLANs to a few instances.

rows.req: Track a link's delay and switch routes when it degrades
rows.why: IP SLA probes the path; tie it to a tracked route.

rows.req: Record which hosts talk to which, and how much
rows.why: Flexible NetFlow exports flow records for analysis.

rows.req: Rate-limit traffic headed to the router's CPU
Save show output to flash automatically when an interface goes down
rows.why: An EEM applet triggers on the event and runs commands.

keep.text: Renew with 80 CE credits, or by passing one core exam, two concentration exams, or one concentration exam plus 40 CE credits. Passing a CCIE lab also works.
keep.after: Recertifying CCNP also renews the associate and specialist certs under it.
